newsitem.title: USA: American Electric in power pact with Ormet.
newsitem.headline: American Electric in power pact with Ormet.

text.p: American Electric Power Co said it filed with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio Thursday to continue as the energy supplier for Ormet Primary Aluminum Corp's Hannibal, Ohio, smelter through 1999.

The two companies have agreed to an interim power contract with AEP continuing to supply electricity to meet the Hannibal site's 536-megawatt around-the-clock demand through the end of 1999, American Electric said.
In a separate joint filing, AEP and South Central Power, an electric distribution cooperative, have proposed changing Ormet's electricity provider at the end of that contract.

AEP and South Central ask for approval to reallocate their service territories effective at 2400 EST December 31, 1999/0500 GMT January 1, 2000, to eliminate an overlap. Following the reallocation, Ormet would be supplied by South Central, which already provides electricity to a portion of the facility and has territory contiguous with the Hannibal site, American Electric explained.

"With our strong track record of marketing electricity to wholesale customers, we are confident that we will find willing buyers for the electricity which will be made available once the interim contract with Ormet ends," said William J. Lhota, executive vice president with AEP.
The territorial reallocation plan and bridging contract are the result of lengthy negotiations in preparation for the 1997 expiration of Ormet's present 30-year power agreement with AEP, it said.
This solution "will not lead to stranded investment on AEP's part," it pointed out..

Ohio law certifies service territories for utilities and does not allow customers to select a supplier, although proposals for deregulation are being reviewed by the Ohio legislature. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
